_comment: 50.T50.03 — the ONE cross-language VakAddress parity fixture. Read by BOTH sides: the TS mirror test (Body/S/S4/ta-onta/S4-4p-anima/tests/vak_orchestration_surface.test.ts) validates every case against ta-onta/shared/vak_address.ts, and the Rust test (Body/S/S0/portal-core/tests/vak_address_ts_parity.rs) deserializes the same cases into portal_core::VakAddress with serde. Neither side greps the other's source: parity is proven by both accepting or both rejecting the identical bytes. Add a case here to bind a new coordinate value across languages.

rejected.name: epi-cli-loose-vak-coordinates
rejected.why: `epi agent vak evaluate` (Body/S/S0/epi-cli/src/agent/vak.rs) emits this separate loose VakCoordinates shape. It is NOT the canonical envelope: cpf is a C-family label rather than a review polarity, cp lacks its 4.x position, ct is a scalar rather than an array, and cs is flat rather than a { code, direction } field. Kept here so both languages agree it is refused rather than silently coerced.

rejected.name: unprimed-night-direction
rejected.why: The Night pass is canonically primed (Night'). An unprimed "Night" is phase-erasing and must not round-trip.

rejected.name: non-canonical-context-frame
rejected.why: (4/5/0) is not one of the seven canonical context frames.
